name: 4-chloroethcathinone
summary: 4-Chloroethcathinone (4-CEC) is an organic chemical compound that is classified as substituted cathinone a stimulant and also probably entactogen. Like other 4-chlorocathinones, it may have the potential for abuse in humans and cause adverse effects similar to those associated with mephedrone. 4-CEC was encountered as a novel designer drug in Europe in 2016.

pharmacology.text: In studies evaluating rat brain synaptosomes in vitro, 4-CEC demonstrated a strong preference for interacting with the serotonin transporter (SERT) over the dopamine transporter (DAT) and norepinephrine transporter (NET). It acts as a moderate SERT reuptake inhibitor and weak reuptake inhibitor at DAT and NET, while functioning as a substrate at SERT. It behaves primarily as a serotonin-releasing agent with weak norepinephrine release profile.
pharmacology.kind: Stimulant; Entactogen; Serotonin releasing agent or serotonin–dopamine releasing agent
